Motivation letter

Certificate of diplomas and degrees already obtained (e.g. Bachelor degree) — in French or English only; otherwise an officially certified French/English translation
University academic transcript of records — in French or English only; otherwise an officially certified French/English translation
Proof of enrollment for the current year (in French or English)
Program-specific additional documents where required (e.g. research project, language certificates, letters of recommendation); if a document is unavailable, a PDF explanation is expected

timeline.resultsBy: Mid-March 2026

benefits: Ampère Scholarship of Excellence: €1,000 per month for 12 months (one academic year), renewable under conditions
Eligible for all ENS de Lyon Master's programs (Exact Sciences, Arts, Human & Social Sciences), except FEADéP and a few excluded master's programs
Paid in three installments: end of October (4 months), end of February (4 months), end of May (4 months)
Related GRADUATE+ Scholarship (separate award, SFRI-funded): €1,000/month for 10 months for selected Graduate initiatives (CORE, DynLifeSys, MathInfi, PACE) in M1 or M2
mustKnow: Living stipend only — €1,000/month is a merit grant; the official sources do NOT state that tuition, travel, insurance, or accommodation are covered. It is not a comprehensive tuition+stipend package.
One application form covers BOTH the Master's admission and the scholarship — there is no separate scholarship application; awards are decided by the ENS de Lyon admission committee.
Route by status: a Bangladeshi applies as a 'non-European student with a higher education degree in a foreign country'. Applying on the wrong form means the application is not considered.
Awarded for one predetermined Master's program for an initial 12 months; renewable under conditions (e.g. into the second master's year) but renewal is not automatic.

Strict obligations while funded: must complete full registration and submit proof before 20 September, sign attendance sheets (1st Tuesday of October, December, February and May), attend all classes/exams, sit resit sessions; failure or unjustified absence stops the stipend AND can trigger repayment of sums already received.

Mobility restrictions: scholarship holders must NOT do a study/research period abroad and must NOT do an internship in a lab not affiliated to ENS de Lyon; internships in the student's own country of origin are never authorized.

Language: certificates of English and/or French level are required depending on the discipline/level; waived if you studied entirely in a French- or English-speaking country (attach a self-written explanation).
As of 2026-06 the 2026-2027 cycle is CLOSED (deadline was 23 Jan 2026); the 2027-2028 calendar is due to be published in November 2026.
No age limit is stated anywhere in the official ENS de Lyon Ampère rules or application pages (any '≤26 / born after 1 January' figure could not be verified and is omitted).

duration: 1 academic year initially (12 months), renewable under conditions for the second master's year
eligibleNationalities: Open to international students with no country exclusions. Bangladeshi nationals are eligible and apply via the 'non-European student with a higher education degree in a foreign country' route. (European = EEA/EU + Norway/Iceland/Liechtenstein/Switzerland/Monaco/Andorra nationals; everyone else, including Bangladesh, is non-European.)
languageRequirements: Certificate of English and/or French level required depending on discipline and study level (per ENS de Lyon reference grids). Exception/waiver if you studied in a French- or English-speaking country or your studies were made entirely in French or English — attach a self-written explanation.
applicationFee: Free (no application fee mentioned)
monthlyStipend: €1,000 per month (12 months for Ampère)
bondObligation: None (no return-home service bond); however, while funded the holder must not study/research abroad or intern outside ENS de Lyon-affiliated labs, and never in their country of origin
renewalConditions: Initial 12 months; renewable under conditions. Continued payment requires full registration, attendance (signed attendance sheets in Oct/Dec/Feb/May), sitting all exams (including resits), and compliance with the Ampère rules and ENS de Lyon internal regulations; breaches stop the stipend and may require repayment.

name: Anne van den Ban Fund (ABF) — Wageningen University & Research
requiredDocuments: There is NO separate ABF application — candidates are selected only from accepted new MSc students; you must first complete a Wageningen University MSc application by the deadline and gain unconditional admission, then the fund selects by invitation
MSc application: bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in its original language + a certified English translation when the original language is other than English or Dutch
MSc application: original complete/up-to-date transcript of academic records (with a sworn translation if not in English or Dutch)
MSc application: proof of English language proficiency (one of the official tests accepted by Wageningen University, unless exempted)
MSc application: Curriculum Vitae / brief personal history (maximum two pages, in English)
MSc application: personal statement (optional, e.g. if the relevance of your transcript/degree is unclear)

timeline.opens: MSc applications for the September 2026 intake (open in the standard WUR admission cycle)
timeline.deadline: 1 February 2026 (MSc application deadline; ABF candidates are selected only from applicants assessed via this deadline)
timeline.resultsBy: 7 May 2026 (selection results communicated to selected candidates only); offers are made in spring, around May. If you have not received an offer by 1 June, you have not been selected.
timeline.notes: Dates are for academic year 2026-2027 / September 2026 intake, as published on WUR's official 'Master's scholarships' page (accessed 2026-06-18). Anchored as of 2026-06: this is the most recent published cycle; the 2027-2028 cycle had not opened. ABF has no direct application — apply for a WUR MSc by 1 February 2026, secure unconditional admission, then await a possible invitation.

benefits: Full or partial scholarship towards an MSc at Wageningen University & Research (the fund explicitly offers both full AND partial scholarships)
Tuition fee covered in full or in part depending on the award
Possible contribution to living costs (award is combined with the WU Fellowship Programme; other income sources are taken into account)
Awarded for the duration of the MSc programme (up to 24 months)
mustKnow: INVITATION-ONLY: you cannot apply directly to the fund. You must first apply for a WUR MSc by 1 February 2026 and gain UNCONDITIONAL admission; the board then selects candidates once a year from accepted new students (offers in spring, around May).
TWO-STEP: step 1 = secure a WUR MSc admission; step 2 = be selected/invited for the scholarship. No separate scholarship form exists.

NOT GUARANTEED FULL FUNDING: awards are explicitly 'full AND partial' — many are partial and may cover tuition only or in part. Other income (other scholarships, earmarked donations, family support, personal income) is weighed in selection, so you may need to top up living costs.
Combined with the WU Fellowship Programme; for the September start only — not offered to students already enrolled in Wageningen on a one-year scholarship.

Open to students from developing / low-income countries (Bangladesh qualifies); this is distinct from WUR's NL Scholarship, whose closed country list does NOT include Bangladesh — do not confuse the two.
The fund's stated intent is that graduates return to their home country after graduation; there is no contractual bond.
If you have not received an offer by 1 June, you have not been selected.
Sibling WUR invitation scholarships (Excellence, ASP) require GPA ≥ 80% / First Class honours; strong academics materially help an ABF invitation, though ABF's own GPA threshold is not published.

universities: Wageningen University & Research

duration: Up to 24 months (the duration of the MSc programme)
eligibleNationalities: International students from developing / low-income countries who have secured unconditional admission to a WUR MSc programme. Bangladesh, as a developing/low-income South Asian country, is not on any exclusion list and qualifies. Not for students already studying in Wageningen on a one-year scholarship; this is a separate award from WUR's NL Scholarship (which has a closed country list that excludes Bangladesh).
languageRequirements: Standard Wageningen MSc English-language requirement applies (an accepted English test such as IELTS/TOEFL unless exempted); ABF itself adds no separate language test. Check WUR's 'English language proficiency MSc' page for the exact minimum scores.
standardizedTests: Not required (no GRE/GMAT for WUR MSc admission)
minGPA: Good academic results / outstanding students are required, but WUR does not publish a fixed ABF GPA cut-off. (Sibling WUR invitation scholarships — Excellence, ASP — require a GPA of 80% or higher / First Class honours; ABF favours strong students but its own threshold is not published.)
applicationFee: No separate ABF application fee (it is invitation-only). The standard WUR MSc application page lists no application fee.
fundingCovers: Tuition fee (in full or in part — full and partial scholarships both exist)
Possible contribution to living costs (combined with the WU Fellowship Programme; other income sources are taken into account)
bondObligation: Not a contractual bond, but the fund's stated purpose is that graduates return to their home country to contribute there after graduation.
renewalConditions: Awarded for the MSc programme duration; continuation depends on satisfactory study progress (per the WU Fellowship Programme framework). No public per-credit renewal threshold is published by WUR.
postStudyWork: The Netherlands offers a post-study 'orientation year' (zoekjaar) residence permit for graduates of Dutch higher education; however the fund's purpose is that graduates return to their home country.

name: ARES International Training Scholarships (Bourses de formations internationales) — Wallonia-Brussels Federation, Belgium
requiredDocuments: 2 letters of recommendation (academic and/or professional)
Original copies of diplomas
Original copies of transcripts of records for all years
Proof of professional occupation for the last 5 years
Nationality certificate or copy of passport
Pre-project (for certain programmes — see the admission conditions specific to each programme)

timeline.deadline: 2025-09-19 (12:00 Belgian time, UTC+1) via the GIRAF platform
timeline.resultsBy: June 2026
timeline.notes: Dates are for the 2026-2027 academic-year cycle (call opened 4 Aug 2025, closed 19 Sep 2025). As of 2026-06 this is the most recent published cycle; the 2027-2028 call had not yet opened. A separate deadline of 12 Sep 2025 16:00 applied to requests to create/validate new GIRAF accounts.

benefits: Monthly subsistence allowance for 12 months, plus a reduced 13th month (for advanced bachelor's/master's degrees)
Round-trip international air travel in economy class on an IATA airline, maximum one return trip per academic year
Insurance fees paid directly by ARES
Visa-related costs (included in the subsistence allowance; amounts above 200 EUR reimbursed on justified real costs)
Inter-institution travel costs up to a maximum of 250 EUR (on justified real costs)
mustKnow: TARGETED AT WORKING PROFESSIONALS FROM 31 PARTNER DEVELOPING COUNTRIES: you must be a permanent resident of and work in one of the 31 eligible countries (exception: Palestinian nationals are eligible even if not residing there). Eligible countries: South Africa, Benin, Bolivia, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cambodia, Cameroon, Cuba, Ecuador, Ethiopia, Haiti, Indonesia, Kenya, Madagascar, Mali, Morocco, Mozambique, Nepal, Niger, Uganda, Peru, Philippines, DR Congo, Guinea (Conakry), Rwanda, Senegal, Tanzania, Palestinian Territory, Tunisia, Vietnam, Zimbabwe.
Minimum 2 years of relevant professional experience after the Bac+5 (for the master de spécialisation track) is required — this is NOT for fresh graduates.

DEGREE-RECENCY RULE (often mis-reported as an age limit): you must have held the relevant academic degree for a maximum of 20 years at the start of the programme (extended by one year per childbirth and/or adoption). There is no stated age limit in the official document.
For the master de spécialisation, you must hold a degree comparable to a Belgian 2nd-cycle diploma (300 ECTS / Bac+5).
You do NOT need to secure admission to a Belgian institution before applying — ARES handles placement (no two-step admission-first process).
Applications are submitted ONLY online via the GIRAF platform; you may apply for one programme only.
Applying is FREE — ARES never requests any payment at any stage; report anyone claiming to act for ARES and requesting payment.
The dossier must be completed in the language of instruction (French for most programmes) with proof of good written and spoken knowledge of it.

Selection weighs the candidate's guarantees of returning to their home/other country and reintegrating professionally to apply the training for development — a knowledge-transfer/return expectation (a selection criterion, not a formal contractual bond).
These are 1-year inter-institutional 'specialization' (de spécialisation) bachelor's/master's programmes, plus 2-6 month continuing-education courses — not standard 2-year master's degrees.

The official document does NOT separately list tuition/registration fees in its funding table; the commonly-cited 1,150 EUR/month stipend figure is from third-party sites, not the official ARES document.

duration: 1 academic year (master/advanced bachelor de spécialisation); 2-6 months for continuing-education programmes
eligibleNationalities: Nationals who are permanent residents of and work in one of 31 ARES partner countries (South Africa, Benin, Bolivia, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cambodia, Cameroon, Cuba, Ecuador, Ethiopia, Haiti, Indonesia, Kenya, Madagascar, Mali, Morocco, Mozambique, Nepal, Niger, Uganda, Peru, Philippines, DR Congo, Guinea-Conakry, Rwanda, Senegal, Tanzania, Palestinian Territory, Tunisia, Vietnam, Zimbabwe); Palestinian nationals eligible even if resident elsewhere
languageRequirements: Application dossier must be completed in the language of instruction (French for most programmes), with proof of good written and spoken knowledge of that language. No specific IELTS/TOEFL band stated.
applicationFee: Free
bondObligation: No formal contractual bond; however, the candidate's guarantees of returning home and applying the training for development are a selection criterion
postStudyWork: Not stated; programme expects return to home/partner country to apply acquired skills for development

Citizens of the Czech Republic/EU and foreign nationals with Czech permanent residence are NOT eligible; there is no legal claim to the award.
Return-home requirement: applicants must sign an Affirmation on Return to the Sending Country upon Completion of Studies.

English-taught follow-up Master's are open to all eligible countries; Czech-taught Master's are limited to applicants from Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Ukraine and Belarus and require a one-year Czech preparatory course.

University entrance examinations may be required and successful passing is a precondition for the scholarship award.
A legalised, recently dated medical certificate (Annex No. 4) is mandatory; documents generally need legalised Czech (or English) translations by a sworn translator.
Stipend amount is 'regularly amended' — the binding Guidelines cite CZK 14,000/month for Master's, but the precise current figure is fixed in each year's annual offer.
Graduates of a Master's programme cannot be awarded a scholarship to study at the same or lower level.

name: DAAD EPOS - Development-Related Postgraduate Courses
requiredDocuments: Completed and signed DAAD application form(s) (you may apply for up to three EPOS-listed courses; list them in order of priority)
Curriculum vitae in reverse chronological order without unexplained gaps (Europass template), with exact information about studies and practical experience

One Letter of Motivation with detailed academic, professional and personal reasons for applying (if applying to more than one course, justify the choice and prioritisation of courses in a single uniform letter)
Letter of recommendation from your current employer (official letterhead, signature, official stamp, current date, not in a sealed envelope)

Certificate(s) of Employment proving at least two years of relevant work experience after the Bachelor's degree up to the time of application (ideally including a guarantee of re-employment on return home)
Recent proof of language skills: English (IELTS or TOEFL — institutional TOEFL not accepted) or German (required for German-taught courses)
Copies of higher-education degree certificates (certified translation if not in German or English)
Copy of full set of transcript of records (with an explanation of the grading system if not included)
APS Certificate (required only for applicants from the People's Republic of China)

timeline.deadline: Varies by chosen EPOS-listed course (no single global deadline). Example: MIDE at HTW Berlin closes 31 August 2025 for a 1 April 2026 start.
timeline.notes: EPOS has no single DAAD deadline — you apply directly to the master's course and each course sets its own deadline (see the official 'List of all Postgraduate courses with application deadlines 2027/28' PDF). The DAAD selection process for all listed courses runs from end of October to March. As of 2026-06 the documented cycle is the 2026/2027 academic year from the official EPOS programme brochure; the deadlines list referenced on the page covers 2027/28 courses. Always check the individual course website/brochure for the exact, current deadline.

benefits: Monthly stipend of 992 EUR for graduate (master's) scholarship holders (1,300 EUR, rising to 1,400 EUR from February 2026, for doctoral candidates)
Payments towards health, accident and personal-liability insurance cover
Travel allowance, unless covered by the home country or another funding source
Possible monthly rent subsidy (under certain circumstances)
Possible monthly allowance for accompanying family members (under certain circumstances)
Tuition exemption/waiver at EPOS-listed courses for DAAD scholarship holders (handled per course)
For German-taught courses, an included preparatory German language course (2-6 months) in Germany before the study course begins
mustKnow: You apply DIRECTLY to a specific EPOS-listed master's course, NOT to the DAAD. Applications sent to the DAAD are not forwarded. You may apply to up to three courses, ranked by priority.

Two-step process: (1) apply to the course; (2) a selection committee proposes candidates; (3) DAAD then invites the proposed candidates to upload their complete documents to the DAAD Portal; (4) final selection. Keep PDF copies of every document ready for the portal upload.
Work-experience gate: you need a Bachelor's degree (usually a four-year course) PLUS at least two years of relevant professional experience after the Bachelor's, up to the application deadline.
Recency rule: academic degrees should normally be no more than six years old at the time of application.
Residency exclusion: applicants who have lived in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline cannot be considered.

Nationality gate: open only to nationals on the OECD-DAC developing-country list supported by EPOS (Bangladesh is included — confirmed under 'South and Central Asia' in the official DAC list, validity 2024-2025); a few DAC countries are explicitly excluded (Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia incl. Kosovo, Turkey).
Development-related motivation is assessed: typical holders work in a public authority or a state/private company in a developing country on development-policy planning/projects.
Funded by Germany's Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ); scholarship announcement depends on BMZ funds being provided.
Fully funded with a living stipend (not tuition-only): stipend + insurance + travel, with tuition exempted/waived per EPOS course for DAAD scholars.

universities: Selected German state or state-recognised universities and universities of applied sciences offering EPOS-listed postgraduate courses (e.g. Universität Leipzig, Universität Stuttgart, Heidelberg, HTW Berlin, MIPLC Munich)

duration: 12 to 42 months depending on the study programme (12-24 months for a master's degree; 40-42 months for a PhD)
intake: Academic year 2026/2027 (intake date set by each EPOS-listed course; e.g. MIDE/HTW Berlin begins 1 April 2026)
eligibleNationalities: Open to graduates from countries on the OECD-DAC developing/newly-industrialised country list supported in the EPOS programme. Bangladesh is included (listed under 'South and Central Asia' in the official DAC list, validity 2024-2025). Excluded DAC countries: Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia (including Kosovo) and Turkey. Applicants resident in Germany longer than 15 months at the deadline are not eligible.
languageRequirements: For English-taught courses: proof of adequate English per the course's regulations (IELTS or TOEFL; institutional TOEFL not accepted). For German-taught courses: DSH 2 or TestDaF 4 before the course starts, with at least German B1 at application (proven by certificate); a 6-month intensive German course in Germany is included but cannot replace prior B1 knowledge.
ageLimit: No fixed age limit, but academic degrees should normally be no more than six years old at the time of application.
applicationFee: No DAAD application fee mentioned; apply directly to the course (course/admission or language-test fees, if any, are separate and not specified by DAAD).
monthlyStipend: 992 EUR per month for graduate (master's) scholarship holders
renewalConditions: Funding runs for the duration of the study programme (12-42 months) contingent on satisfactory academic progress; for German-taught courses, passing DSH 2 / TestDaF 4 is a formal prerequisite for university matriculation.
postStudyWork: Programme expects graduates to return to and apply their skills in their home country/region (development-related objective); a guarantee of re-employment from the current employer is requested where possible.

name: DAAD Hilde Domin Programme (Master's for At-Risk Students)
requiredDocuments: Online nomination form completed by the nominating German institution/organisation (candidate cannot self-apply)
Questionnaire on the nominee's risk situation ('Risk description form') submitted as part of the nomination
Proof or credible demonstration of a threat to personal well-being or safety (e.g. physical violence, arrest, denial of civil/educational rights) provided to the nominating institution
Educational certificates enabling entrance to a German higher education institution (recognised per the anabin database)
Language certificate showing German or English at B2 level as required by the intended degree programme
Valid passport (still valid for at least one year on the DAAD application deadline; accompanying spouse/minor children must also hold valid passports)
Application via the DAAD online application portal after being invited following nomination (documents submitted in German or English)
For visual/performing arts, design, visual communication, music, film, architecture: a letter from an accredited higher-education institution confirming academic ability and willingness to enrol

timeline.opens: Nominations can be submitted online at any time; DAAD candidate application periods: 17 March - 15 April 2026 (summer semester 2027) and 17 September - 15 October 2026 (winter semester 2027/28)
timeline.deadline: Nominations by 15 March 2026 for summer semester 2027 start; nominations by 15 September 2026 for winter semester 2027/28 start
timeline.notes: Dates are the two cycles published on the official DAAD page as of 2026-06. The summer-semester-2027 nomination/application windows have already closed; the winter-semester-2027/28 windows (nominations by 15 Sep 2026, DAAD application 17 Sep - 15 Oct 2026) are the next open ones. Candidates do not apply directly - they are nominated, then invited by DAAD to apply within the application window. Nominating institutions run their own internal deadlines (e.g. TUM requires a nomination request 17-30 Aug 2026 for the winter 2027/28 round).

benefits: Monthly scholarship payment of currently 992 EUR for master's students (1,400 EUR for doctoral candidates)
Health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Travel allowance based on country of origin / present residence
If applicable, a preparatory German language course (2, 4 or 6 months) according to required language skills
Additional financial benefits
Funding for up to 24 months for a master's degree
Qualification through participation in interdisciplinary trainings

acceptanceRate.estimateNote: No acceptance/selection rate is published by DAAD. The DAAD page states 'The DAAD can only award a limited number of scholarships' and TUM's official page notes 'Demand usually greatly exceeds the number of scholarships available' - qualitative only, not a numeric rate.

mustKnow: You CANNOT self-apply: candidates must be nominated by the management of a German legal entity active in science/research/teaching and/or human-rights protection, peace, democracy or rule of law. Only after an initial DAAD plausibility check are suitable candidates invited to apply via the DAAD portal.

This is a protection programme for people at risk: you must prove or credibly demonstrate a personal threat (e.g. physical violence, arrest, denial of civil/educational rights) due to ethnic, sexual, gender or religious identity and/or political or civic engagement. Both risk status AND academic prospects are assessed.
Worldwide eligibility EXCEPT nationals of EU/EEA/EFTA countries, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino and the United Kingdom - Bangladesh is NOT excluded, so Bangladeshis are eligible.
You may NOT already be residing in Germany or the European Union at the time of nomination.
German or English at B2 level (matching the intended programme's language) is required by the nomination deadline.
Human medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine, pharmacy and law are excluded disciplines; a second master's or doctoral degree is not funded.

TUITION IS NOT GUARANTEED: the scholarship covers a living stipend and insurance, not university tuition. At fee-charging universities (e.g. TUM, where non-EEA master's tuition is generally EUR 3,000 or EUR 6,000) DAAD does NOT pay the fees - apply for a waiver or choose a tuition-free university. Most German public universities charge no tuition.
Two-step process: a DAAD scholarship confirmation does NOT secure a study place - you must separately apply for and be admitted to a degree programme by the host university within its own deadlines.
Passport must be valid for at least one year on the DAAD application deadline (also for any accompanying spouse/minor children).
Multiple nominations give no advantage; one nomination per candidate suffices. Nominations via email/post/fax are not accepted.

universities: Any recognised higher education institution in Germany (degree programme of personal choice; e.g. Technical University of Munich)

duration: Up to 24 months for a master's degree
eligibleNationalities: Open to students/doctoral candidates worldwide who are at risk in their country of origin, EXCEPT nationals of EU/EEA/EFTA countries, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino and the United Kingdom. Bangladeshi nationals are eligible.
languageRequirements: German or English at B2 level (corresponding to the language of the intended programme) by the nomination deadline; the required language certificate for the specific degree programme must be provided.
applicationFee: Free (no application fee; application is via the DAAD portal after nomination)
monthlyStipend: 992 EUR per month (master's students)
bondObligation: None stated. The programme's long-term goal is for beneficiaries to contribute to development in their country of origin, in Germany or in third countries after completing studies, but no binding return/service obligation is imposed.

name: DAAD Study Scholarships - Master Studies for Graduates of All Disciplines
requiredDocuments: Full curriculum vitae in tabular form (max. 3 pages)
Letter of motivation: statement about academic and personal reasons for the planned study project in Germany (1-3 pages)
Letter of admission to the study programme at the host university in Germany (if not yet received at time of application, must be submitted before the funding period begins)
Form 'Information about your preferred master programmes' (if planning a second degree or Master's programme in Germany)
Proof that credits acquired in Germany will be recognised by your home university (if studying in Germany as part of a degree abroad)
Current overview of grades / transcript of records with individual grades
University degree certificate indicating final grade(s) (must be submitted by the time funding starts if not yet completed at application)
Proof of knowledge of the language(s) of instruction (no older than 3 years; e.g. TestDaF/DSH for German, IELTS/TOEFL for English)
One recent letter of recommendation from a university teacher (generated as a form in the DAAD portal)
Optional: other relevant documents (e.g. certificates of employment, proof of extracurricular engagement)

timeline.deadline: Country-specific (set per applicant's country of origin; no single global date)
timeline.notes: Applications open annually on 1 June; for this round the funding period must begin in 2027 and the scholarship usually begins 1 October 2027. The application deadline is set per applicant's country of origin and is only shown in the DAAD portal during the active application window, so there is no single global deadline date. Deadlines are updated annually in the second quarter and are usually in the same period as the previous year. Funding is only available for degree programmes starting in the winter semester of the following year.

benefits: Monthly scholarship payment of EUR 992 for Master's students
Annual study allowance of EUR 460
Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover (DAAD usually takes out private health insurance and pays the premiums)
Flat-rate travel allowance (upon application)
Funding for a German language course (2, 4 or 6 months) before the study visit where appropriate; payment of online language course fees; reimbursement of TestDaF or DSH test fees

Possible additional benefits after start of funding: monthly rent subsidy; monthly allowance for accompanying family members (partner allowance EUR 276/month, child allowance EUR 259/month per child); disability/chronic-illness subsidy; Green Mobility top-up for climate-friendly travel
mustKnow: Tuition NOT covered: DAAD does not pay tuition fees. German public universities are generally tuition-free, but exceptions exist - Baden-Wuerttemberg charges EUR 1,500/semester for non-EU/EEA students and TU Munich charges EUR 4,000-6,000/semester for Master's programmes; these are not reimbursed.

Aimed in particular at applicants from industrial countries. Students from developing/emerging countries are steered to other DAAD programmes such as 'Study scholarships for STEM disciplines' and EPOS (Development-related Postgraduate Courses).

Two-step in practice: you are responsible for securing your own admission to a German university; a valid Letter of Admission to the named host programme is required before the funding period begins, and the DAAD Award Letter is only valid if you have been admitted.

Degree recency rule: as a rule your most recent university degree should not date back more than 6 years at the time of the application deadline (exceptions for childcare, illness, military service, etc.).
Residence rule: your application cannot be considered if you have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline.
Language proof of the language of instruction (German and/or English; no older than 3 years) is required when applying to DAAD; IELTS/TOEFL (English) or TestDaF/DSH (German) are accepted.

Funding period is 10 to 24 months (standard period of study, max 24 months); funding must begin in 2027 (scholarship usually starts 1 October 2027) and cannot fund a Master's already started in Germany.
Application deadline is country-specific and only appears in the portal during the active window (applications open 1 June).

universities: Any state or state-recognised university in Germany

duration: 10 to 24 months (standard period of study, max 24 months)
eligibleNationalities: Aimed in particular at applicants from industrial countries; eligibility and deadlines vary by country of origin (you must select your status and country to apply). Applicants from developing/emerging countries are directed to other DAAD programmes (STEM, EPOS).
languageRequirements: Proof of proficiency in the language of instruction (German and/or English), no older than 3 years. Accepted English certificates include IELTS, TOEFL iBT, Cambridge English, PTE Academic, Duolingo English Test; accepted German certificates include TestDaF, DSH, Goethe-Zertifikat, telc Deutsch.
ageLimit: No fixed age limit; instead a degree-recency rule (most recent degree generally not older than 6 years at the application deadline).
applicationFee: No application fee mentioned for the DAAD scholarship application (university language certificates and admission may incur separate fees not reimbursed by DAAD).
monthlyStipend: EUR 992 per month (Master's students)
bondObligation: None stated (scholarships do not have to be repaid)
renewalConditions: After the first year of study, academic achievements are assessed; if you are on track to complete within a reasonable period, funding continues as planned.

name: ENS-PSL International Selection (École Normale Supérieure - PSL)
requiredDocuments: Detailed editable application form (downloaded from ENS, filled out)
High school diploma (in French or English; Spanish, Italian or Portuguese also accepted)
University transcript (in French or English; Spanish, Italian or Portuguese also accepted)
Curriculum vitae (CV)

Motivation/cover letter, 1 to 3 pages (Times New Roman, 12 pt, 1.5 spacing) — in French for Arts & Humanities (also in English for Economics, Linguistics, Cognitive studies); in French OR English for Sciences
Arts & Humanities only: a research/study project of max 3 pages (10,000 characters incl. spaces) with a bibliography of 10 books
2 to 4 letters of recommendation (any format accepted)
All documents merged into a single PDF named 'Family Name-Given Name.pdf' (do NOT include a passport or ID card)

timeline.deadline: Arts & Humanities: 3 December 2025, 12:00 midday Paris time; Sciences: 15 December 2025, 12:00 midday Paris time
timeline.resultsBy: Admission results from 4 March 2026 (Arts & Humanities) / from 26 March 2026 (Sciences)
timeline.notes: Dates are the 2026-entry cycle (applications Oct–Dec 2025), as published on the official page (last updated 18/02/2026). As of the 2026-06 anchor the next cycle had not opened; the program runs on a fixed annual calendar (apply in autumn, tests Feb–Mar, entry in autumn). Shortlist/tests: A&H written tests 2–6 Feb 2026 and oral tests 9–13 Feb 2026; Sciences tests 3–20 March 2026 — all conducted remotely by videoconference.

benefits: Monthly grant of €1,000 paid for 36 months (3 years)
Right to request a furnished room on an ENS campus (rue d'Ulm, boulevard Jourdan, or Montrouge); rent ~€315/month
Tuition in French public universities paid by the French State (student pays only modest annual registration/inscription fees + CVEC)
Free French language courses throughout the year, plus an intensive course at the start of September
Graduate with both a Master's degree (M1+M2) in the chosen specialty and the diploma of the École normale supérieure (DENS)

acceptanceRate.source: ENS-PSL official FAQ: 'How hard is the selection? The selection rates varies from year to year, between 5 and 10%.' https://www.ens.psl.eu/en/une-formation-d-exception/admissions/international/international-selection/faq-about-international (accessed 2026-06-18)

mustKnow: Strict age limit: you must apply before turning 26 (Arts & Humanities: not past your 26th birthday on 1 December; Sciences: under 26 on the application opening day).
Two-step competitive examination: first a selection on dossier, then remote (videoconference) written and oral tests for shortlisted candidates — this is a concours, not a simple admissions review.
You can apply to the International Selection ONLY ONCE in your life — former candidates' files are not transmitted to the jury.

Requires at least one year of undergraduate study at a FOREIGN (non-French) university now, and two years by the September after admission — a Bangladeshi who studied in Bangladesh qualifies; there is no nationality restriction.
Residence rule: must not have lived in France more than 10 months (Arts & Humanities) / 6 months (Sciences) during the selection year and the year before.

Fully funded with a living stipend (€1,000/month for 36 months) PLUS state-paid tuition — but the grant is not paid during any gap year, and ENS can only pay it into a French bank account you must open on arrival.

No ten-year State-service commitment: International Selection students receive a grant (not a salary) and do not become civil servants, so unlike regular normaliens they are NOT bound by the ten-year engagement — effectively no return-home/service bond.

Arts & Humanities is taught and tested mainly in French (B1 reading/writing recommended, no official certificate required); Sciences departments teach in French or English and no language level is officially required — so no IELTS/TOEFL is demanded.
Enrollment in both a Master's and the ENS graduate degree (DENS, 72 extra ECTS over 3 years) is compulsory.

universities: École Normale Supérieure - PSL (Université PSL)

duration: 3 years (M1+M2 Master plus 72 ECTS for the ENS graduate degree / DENS)
eligibleNationalities: Open to all nationalities worldwide (no country restriction); requires at least one year (ultimately two years) of undergraduate study at a foreign/non-French university and a France-residence cap. Bangladeshi nationals are eligible.
languageRequirements: No official language certificate required. Arts & Humanities: courses and most tests in French — candidates should read/write French at roughly B1 level. Sciences: courses in French or English depending on department; no language level officially required. No IELTS/TOEFL demanded.
standardizedTests: Not required (selection is via ENS's own written and oral competitive tests, not GRE/GMAT)
ageLimit: Under 26 — must apply before turning 26 (Arts & Humanities: not past 26th birthday on 1 December; Sciences: under 26 on opening day of applications)
applicationFee: Free (no application fee stated on the official page)
fundingCovers: On-campus accommodation (room available, rent ~€315/month paid from grant)
Tuition (state-paid; only modest annual registration/inscription fees + CVEC remain)
monthlyStipend: €1,000 per month for 36 months
bondObligation: None — International Selection students receive a grant (not a salary), do not become civil servants, and are not subject to the ten-year State-service commitment.
renewalConditions: Grant paid over 3 years; must remain enrolled in a Master's and the ENS graduate degree (DENS, 72 ECTS over 3 years). Grant is suspended during any gap year/semester (up to 2 gap years permitted).
postStudyWork: Graduates hold a French Master's degree plus the ENS diploma; standard French post-study work/residence options apply (admitted students enter on a 'visa long séjour pour études' arranged via Campus France). No program-specific stay-back scheme stated.

Internal EPFL candidates changing field: same documents required for admission plus two recommendation letters from professors (sent directly by referees)

timeline.deadline: External candidates: 1st round December 15, 2nd round March 31
timeline.resultsBy: Beginning of April (1st round); early to mid-June (2nd round)
timeline.notes: Deadlines as published on the official how-to-apply page as accessed 2026-06-06; they are recurring annual dates aligned with the EPFL Master application. External-candidate deadlines are December 15 and March 31; internal EPFL candidates have separate rounds (January 31 / April 15).

benefits: CHF 10,000 per semester, for a maximum of 4 semesters
Guaranteed reservation of a student room in a student residence (external candidates only)
Certificate of excellence upon completion of the Master's program

acceptanceRate.estimateNote: The official FAQ states only that the program is 'very competitive and only a small percentage of applicants is awarded the scholarship'; no numeric rate is published.

mustKnow: NOT fully funded in the tuition+stipend sense: this is a CHF 10,000/semester merit stipend; students remain responsible for all living expenses including tuition fees and rent (tuition is not waived).

No separate application form: you apply by checking the excellence fellowship box on the standard EPFL online Master application (one exception: internal EPFL students in the same field may apply by email).
Covers 2-3 semesters of the Master's cycle plus 1 semester for the Master's project, up to a maximum of 4 semesters (90-credit programs: max 3 semesters).
Renewal for year 2 requires a weighted average of at least 5.0/6 AND at least 50 ECTS credits; no exceptions are made.
Candidates already holding a Master's degree or already enrolled in an EPFL Master's program are not eligible; cannot apply for the 2nd year only.
Deferring or postponing admission forfeits the scholarship (you may reapply the following year).
Cannot be combined with other substantial scholarships; all scholarships received must be declared and each case is reviewed individually.
Paid into a Swiss bank/postal account at the start of each semester; recipients should bring funds for the first month as the initial payment may be delayed.
No minimum GPA to apply; TOEFL/GRE scores are welcome but not compulsory and do not influence evaluation.

universities: École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)

duration: Up to 4 semesters (2 years), including 1 semester for the Master's project
eligibleNationalities: Open to all nationalities; international students may apply provided they meet EPFL Master admission criteria
languageRequirements: Language certificate not compulsory; TOEFL scores welcome but not required and have no influence on fellowship evaluation
standardizedTests: Not required (GRE/TOEFL welcome but not compulsory and not used in evaluation)
minGPA: No minimum GPA to apply; renewal requires weighted average of at least 5.0/6
applicationFee: Not stated on the fellowship pages (standard EPFL Master application applies)

bondObligation: None stated
renewalConditions: Weighted average of at least 5.0/6 and at least 50 ECTS credits earned in the first MA year; no exceptions

name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM) Scholarships
requiredDocuments: Proof of a bachelor's degree (first degree), or proof of being in the final year of bachelor studies and graduating before the master's programme starts
Proof of an officially recognised bachelor's-equivalent level of learning, where applicable

Note: there is no single EU-wide document list — each EMJM consortium publishes its own required documents (typically transcripts, CV, motivation letter, references and, where required, an English-language certificate) on its own programme website

timeline.deadline: Typically January (varies by consortium)
timeline.notes: EMJM is an umbrella programme: there is no single central deadline. Students apply directly to each joint master, and each consortium sets its own opening and closing dates. The official students page states applications are 'in most cases' submitted between October and January for courses starting the following academic year; these dates describe the recurring annual window. As of 2026-06 the October 2025–January 2026 window (for 2026 entry) has closed and the next window (≈October 2026–January 2027, for 2027 entry) had not yet opened — always check the specific master's own website for its exact dates.

benefits: Monthly student scholarship of 1,400 EUR/month for the full duration of the master (12, 18 or 24 months), awarded only to full-time students
Scholarship covers travel, visa, installation and subsistence (living allowance) costs
No tuition fees or other mandatory participation costs charged to scholarship holders; selected projects also cannot charge student application fees
Full insurance coverage for enrolled students (organised via the consortium's institutional grant)
Top-up contribution to individual needs for enrolled students with disabilities (special-needs unit costs ranging from EUR 3,000 up to EUR 60,000)
mustKnow: EMJM is an umbrella action covering many separate joint masters — you apply directly to the institution/consortium running your chosen programme, not to the EU centrally, and each consortium sets its own entry requirements, language tests, documents and deadlines.

'Fully funded' here is genuine: scholarship holders pay no tuition and no application fee and receive a 1,400 EUR/month living allowance plus travel/visa/installation costs and insurance. Non-scholarship (self-funded) admission also exists for most programmes.
Geographical balance rule: no more than 10% of the scholarships awarded over a project may go to candidates of the same nationality (excluding top-up scholarships for targeted regions).
Students who have previously obtained an EMJM scholarship are not eligible to apply for another EMJM scholarship.
You must hold a bachelor's degree (or be in your final bachelor year and graduate before the master starts); a recognised bachelor's-equivalent level may also qualify.
Anti-fraud: the EU never charges a fee to be selected for a scholarship — be wary of any message asking you to pay to receive an EU-funded scholarship.

Since masters selected from 2021, the old Programme/Partner country distinction no longer applies and all students receive the same scholarship; programmes span study at several universities in at least 3 different countries.

universities: Delivered by a consortium of at least 3 higher education institutions from at least 3 different countries (varies per programme)

duration: 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS)
eligibleNationalities: Open to students from all over the world; subject to a 10% per-nationality cap on awarded scholarships per project
applicationFee: Free — selected projects cannot charge student application fees
fundingCovers: Tuition (no fees charged to scholarship holders)
monthlyStipend: 1,400 EUR/month
bondObligation: None

name: Eric Bleumink Fellowship (Talent Grant) — University of Groningen
requiredDocuments: A completed application for admission to a University of Groningen Master's degree programme, resulting in a provisional or unconditional admission offer before February (the fellowship nomination is based on this master's application)
Letters of recommendation confirming excellent academic performance
Evidence of excellent bachelor/undergraduate grades (academic transcripts)
Proof of English language proficiency meeting the admission requirements of the chosen programme
EBF motivation letter — requested only from nominated candidates, to be sent to the Admission Office within one week of nomination
Copies of application forms for any other funding applied for (to be submitted as part of the motivation/selection materials)

timeline.deadline: 1 December 2025 (master's-programme application must be completed by this date to be considered)
timeline.resultsBy: Before 1 March 2026 (EBF selection committee informs all nominees of the outcome)
timeline.notes: There is no separate fellowship application form and no published 'opening' date — candidates are nominated based on their master's application. Process: master's application complete before 1 December; Admission Office selects nominees in the first week of January; nominees notified before 1 February (no contact by 1 February means not nominated); EBF committee makes final selection before 1 March. These are fixed annual dates anchored to the most recent known cycle (1 December 2025 master's deadline -> September 2026 intake). As of 2026-06 the next cycle (1 December 2026 master's deadline, September 2027 intake) had not yet opened. Master's programmes start in September only.

benefits: Full tuition fee for the Master's programme paid by the Eric Bleumink Fellowship
Living allowance of EUR 1250 per month for food and accommodation
Settling-in allowance of EUR 275 for arrival expenses
Study/book allowance of EUR 310 per year for books and study materials
Round-trip international travel (economy class) between the home country's nearest airport and Amsterdam, including travel insurance and airport taxes; train travel within the Netherlands reimbursed
Private health insurance (currently via AON) covering medical treatment, personal accidents, emergency flight home, and private legal liability — premium paid by the fund

acceptanceRate.estimateNote: Not a published rate. The official Rules and Regulations (Nov 2024) state the fellowship 'receives hundreds of applications each year and only four of them will be awarded with a scholarship,' indicating it is highly competitive, but no formal acceptance-rate figure is published.

mustKnow: You CANNOT directly apply for the Eric Bleumink Fellowship. The University of Groningen Admission Office and Faculty Admission Boards nominate suitable candidates based on their master's application; nominees are notified before 1 February, and if not contacted by then you were not selected.
Extremely competitive: the official Rules and Regulations state the fund receives hundreds of applications each year and only four are awarded a scholarship.

Restricted to nationals of least-developed / poorest developing countries listed in Appendix 1 (DAC List of ODA Recipients - Least Developed Countries); applicants from other countries are not eligible.
Master's programmes funded must start in September only (the grant is for 1-year or 2-year master's degrees starting in September).
Applicants must have NO other means of financing the study; holding another University of Groningen scholarship simultaneously with the EBF Talent Grant is not allowed.
Return-home obligation: by accepting the grant, recipients state they will return to their own country at the end of the fellowship / training programme.
Does NOT cover family/dependents — the fellowship does not provide for the cost of bringing or supporting family members in the Netherlands.
Recipients may not enter into paid employment in the Netherlands and must refrain from commercial or political activities.
Must be in good health so that health insurance in the Netherlands can be arranged.
Your master's-programme application must be completed before 1 December and result in (provisional) admission before February to be considered for nomination.

universities: University of Groningen (Rijksuniversiteit Groningen)

duration: 1 or 2 years (depending on the Master's programme)
eligibleNationalities: Only nationals of countries listed in Appendix 1 (DAC List of ODA Recipients - Least Developed / poorest developing countries), e.g. Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Nepal, Rwanda, Uganda, Yemen, Tanzania, Nigeria, Pakistan, Vietnam, Ukraine, Sudan, Zimbabwe and others listed on the official page.
languageRequirements: Excellent English language proficiency in accordance with the admission requirements of the chosen Master's programme (specific IELTS/TOEFL bands depend on the programme).
ageLimit: None stated in the official Rules and Regulations
monthlyStipend: EUR 1250 per month (living allowance for food and accommodation)
bondObligation: Return-home requirement: recipients state, by accepting the grant, that they will return to their own country at the end of the fellowship / training programme.

Extensions are granted only for serious illness, death/serious illness of an immediate relative, or delays beyond the recipient's control.

name: ETH Zurich Excellence Scholarship & Opportunity Programme (ESOP)
requiredDocuments: All standard documents required for ETH Zurich Master admission (submitted via eApply, the online Master application)
A pre-proposal for your Master's thesis, developed by yourself using established scientific citation practice (see ETH 'guidelines_preproposal' PDF)

Two reference letters from reference persons (professors) — required for ESOP; if your study programme does not already ask for references, you must name two professors who will upload reference letters after an email from the system

timeline.deadline: 30 November 2026, 23:59 (MEZ/CET)
timeline.resultsBy: End of March 2027
timeline.notes: As of 2026-06-06 the officially published upcoming application window (1-30 November 2026, for an HS27 / autumn-2027 Master start, with decisions communicated end of March 2027) has not yet opened; these are the most recent dates published on the ETH page. The prior cycle (November 2025) has closed and ETH does not list its dates on this page. Decisions for the 2027/28 academic year start are communicated by end of March.

benefits: Scholarship covering living and study expenses: CHF 12'000 per semester
Full tuition fee waiver for the regular duration of the Master's programme
Awarded for the regular duration of the Master's programme (three or four semesters)
Mentorship and access to the network of the ETH Foundation
Programme is fully funded by donations

acceptanceRate.estimateNote: No applicant-vs-awarded ratio is published. ETH states approximately 60 ESOP scholarships are assigned for the 2027/28 start, and the ETH Foundation states the goal is to award at least 50-60 scholarships per year 'through a highly competitive selection' (52 Excellence Scholars began in September 2025). These are award counts, not an acceptance rate.

mustKnow: Fully funded = living/study stipend (CHF 12'000 per semester) PLUS a tuition fee waiver — not tuition-only.
You are NOT eligible if you are already enrolled in a Master's degree programme at ETH Zurich or already hold a Master degree.
You must apply within the FIRST application window of the Master admission; a separate later ESOP application is not possible.
A self-developed pre-proposal for your Master's thesis is mandatory; plagiarism or misinformation leads to exclusion or revocation of admission and scholarship.
Eligibility expects a very good Bachelor result — top 10% of your Bachelor's programme (grade A), based on self-assessment.
The selection process might include a phone/VC interview in February — you must be reachable on the phone number in your CV.

Highly competitive: only about 50-60 scholarships are awarded per year across all ETH Master's programmes; the exact number depends on availability of donor funds. Does not apply to MAS (Master of Advanced Studies) programmes.

One-year study grant for a master's degree at a German university, renewable yearly up to a maximum of 3 years

4-6 months of German language and culture training in Bonn at the start of the stay (for English-taught programs); language/culture training of four to six months also possible for German-taught programs
Personal, spiritual and academic support plus access to KAAD's worldwide scholar/alumni network and accompanying educational program/seminars

Bangladesh is one of KAAD's six Asia focus countries; applications from non-focus countries are 'only considered in exceptional cases'.

languageRequirements: A language test is required where applicable for the chosen programme; language requirements depend on the programme (some are taught in French, some in English), and the test must match the language of the programme. Test results must be attached directly in the online application by the scholarship application deadline.
applicationFee: €150 application fee (mandatory; non-refundable for incomplete, withdrawn or unsuccessful applications). Fee waivers only for current-year CROUS scholarship holders, applicants with disabilities, applicants with proof of refugee status, or those declared eligible for the Mastercard Foundation Scholarship — these waiver routes do not generally apply to a Bangladeshi applicant.
fundingCovers: Partial tuition-fee exemption (€18,500 per year for Master's, for each of the two years)
renewalConditions: Awarded for the first year of study; the amount is fixed at admission and may be recalculated yearly in line with tuition-fee increases. The scholarship is lost if the student does not validate the academic year or defers admission.
requiredDocuments: Indicate the Émile Boutmy scholarship application in the "Financial information" section of the Sciences Po online application (the scholarship is part of the admissions application — there is no separate form)
Language test results, where applicable for the chosen programme (must be attached by the scholarship deadline)
ID: passport, national ID or residence permit
CV / Résumé
Academic transcript(s) for the entirety of higher education (with name and institution)
Copy of the diploma that qualifies you to apply, if already obtained
Two academic references (except one-year master's and Master in urban planning)
Motivation letter / personal statement, written in the language of the chosen programme
Grade-average certificate (one per degree/institution)
Programme-specific additional documents where required (e.g. GRE, GMAT, copy of law degree)

As of June 2026, the official admissions page states "Admissions for the 2026 intake are closed and reopen next autumn for the 2027 intake," so the next (2027-2028) cycle is expected to open autumn 2026 with comparable October/November scholarship committee deadlines. The scholarship deadline is the same as the admissions deadline; if applying for a scholarship you must meet the earliest deadline. All deadlines refer to Paris time (11:59pm).

benefits: Master's: €18,500 exemption from tuition fees for EACH of the two years of the programme
Awarded on merit and the profile sought for the programme
May be combined with external scholarships (Eiffel, AEFE, French government scholarships)
mustKnow: TUITION-ONLY and PARTIAL — there is no living stipend, travel or insurance. The Master's award (€18,500/year) does not even cover full tuition: non-EEA-resident Master's tuition is €20,640/year (2026-2027), leaving ~€2,140/year plus all Paris living costs for the student to fund.

TWO-STEP: you must first be admitted to an eligible Sciences Po Master's programme; the scholarship is then awarded by the Admissions Department only to admitted students. You cannot apply for the scholarship alone.
Apply WITH your admission application by ticking the Boutmy request in the "Financial information" section — it is NOT possible to apply for the scholarship after admission or during your studies.
First-time applicants only and the household must not file taxes in the EU; tax residence of the parents (not the student) is what counts.

NOT eligible: one-year Master's programmes, the Master's in Journalism and the Joint Master's in Journalism & International Affairs, and most master's-level dual degrees (a few China/Columbia dual degrees excepted).
Cannot be combined with other Sciences Po/partner scholarships (Mastercard, CARE, CSC, etc.), but CAN be combined with external scholarships such as Eiffel.
If you apply for a scholarship you must meet the EARLIEST applicable deadline; incomplete or late files are rejected, and a previous Boutmy refusal in the same admission cycle bars reapplication.
A €150 non-refundable application fee is mandatory; the usual fee-waiver routes (CROUS, disability, refugee, Mastercard) typically do not apply to a Bangladeshi applicant.

name: Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (AMS) — University of Amsterdam

universities: University of Amsterdam (UvA)

duration: 1-2 years (length of the chosen Master's programme; renewed for year 2 in two-year programmes subject to progress)
eligibleNationalities: Open to students holding a non-EU/EEA (and non-Swiss) passport who are not eligible for Dutch study grants/loans (Studiefinanciering). Bangladeshi nationals qualify as non-EU/EEA.
requiredDocuments: Complete admission application to a UvA Master's (MSc/LLM/MA) programme submitted by the deadline (the scholarship application is part of/linked to it)
Tick the box on the application form indicating you want to be considered for a UvA scholarship
Academic records / transcripts of all years of your degree, including your GPA
Curriculum vitae (CV), including extracurricular activities (student commissions, international experience, sport/music at high level, volunteer work)

Letter of motivation (maximum 500 words) explaining choice of programme and the relevance of the scholarship for your future academic career (Faculty of Science requires the AMS rationale to be a paragraph inside this same 500-word letter)

timeline.deadline: 15 January 2026 (Faculty of Science and Amsterdam Law School; Law deadline is 23:59 CET) — deadlines differ per Faculty/Graduate School
timeline.resultsBy: Selection in March; applicants informed by end of March / April (varies by faculty)
timeline.notes: AMS deadlines and award amounts vary per Faculty/Graduate School. Dates here are for the 2026-2027 / September 2026 intake as published on the Faculty of Science and Amsterdam Law School pages (deadline 15 January 2026), and were the published cycle at the 2026-06 anchor. Other faculties (Humanities, Social Sciences, Psychology, Economics & Business, etc.) set their own deadlines and amounts on their own pages — always check the specific faculty page.

benefits: Cash merit grant paid in monthly instalments — Faculty of Science: €24,875 (September 2026 start); Amsterdam Law School: €25,900 (2026-2027). Amount and number of awards vary per faculty.
Intended as a living/study allowance toward costs of studying at UvA
fundingCovers: Monthly cash grant / living allowance (amount varies by faculty)
monthlyStipend: Paid in monthly instalments; total e.g. €24,875 (Science 2026) or €25,900 (Law 2026-2027) per year
minGPA: Top 10% of class. Faculty of Science: ~GPA 3.5 (US 4-pt), UK first-class/upper division, or 8+ (Dutch 10-pt). Amsterdam Law School: comparable to 4.0 (US), UK first-class honours, or 8.0 (Dutch 10-pt).
bondObligation: None
renewalConditions: In two-year Master's programmes, the AMS is renewed for the second year only if the student completes the first year with good results (at least 40 ECTS) and meets faculty/programme requirements (e.g. attendance, good progress).
mustKnow: NOT a tuition waiver and NOT fully funded: the AMS cannot be used as a (partial) tuition fee waiver — recipients must still pay the full tuition fee, and must have sufficient funds to cover all other costs. The grant is a separate cash allowance paid in monthly instalments.

Faculty-specific: award amount, number of scholarships, eligible programmes and deadlines all differ per Faculty/Graduate School — the Faculty of Science page states only ONE AMS is available there for September 2026.
Highly selective merit award: applicants must be in the top 10% of their class (roughly GPA 3.5-4.0 / UK first-class / Dutch 8.0+).

Two-step: you must submit a complete admission application to a UvA Master's AND a scholarship application (or tick the scholarship box) by the deadline; incomplete scholarship applications are not considered.

Eligibility excludes anyone with EU/EEA/Swiss nationality, anyone eligible for Dutch study grants/loans, anyone eligible for the reduced EEA tuition rate, and anyone receiving another full-coverage scholarship for the same period.
Recency rule (Faculty of Science): must have completed the previous academic programme no longer than 3 years ago; must be a first-time Master's applicant/admit at UvA.
Must be able to meet Dutch visa (IND) requirements; notify the international/scholarship team of any change in nationality, residence permit, or additional financial support.
